_frame_plan_note: 960 frames at 30 fps; boundaries sit at the expected beat edges (4.68, 9.51, 14.94, 20.14, 26.45 s); re-measured by the preflight.

shots.visual_proof: A ground-level camera at the bed entrance looks back at the truck charging in head-on at 90 km/h (red BRAKES FAILED warning over the speed read-out, focus following the truck); just before it reaches the gravel a hard cut to a low side view as the tyres hit the stones and gravel and dust explode; then a dolly ahead of the truck and a side-on view of the rear wheels.
shots.narration_en: This truck has lost its brakes, and it is about to plow into a bed of loose gravel.

shots.visual_proof: Macro at the drive wheels: the tyres sit below the surface of the gravel and push a wave of stones aside while the read-out falls.
shots.narration_en: Every wheel sinks into the stones, and digging through them quickly drains the truck's speed.

shots.visual_proof: Cutaway (device): a thin slice of the bed seen side-on with a wheel rolling through it. Big on-screen steps appear in turn: 1 THE WHEEL SINKS IN (the wheel settles into the stones), 2 STONES PILE UP AHEAD (the wheel shoves the stones it meets into a growing pile in front of it, leaving a rut behind), 3 THE PILE PUSHES BACK (a red arrow points back at the wheel).
shots.narration_en: Each wheel must shove a pile of loose stones ahead of it, and the pile pushes back.

shots.visual_proof: Raised tracking view from behind: the truck keeps slowing while a read-out compares gravel drag (0.25 g) with pavement (0.01 g, assumed values).
shots.narration_en: Loose gravel drags at about a quarter of the truck's weight, twenty-five times more than pavement.

shots.visual_proof: Straight-down view: a green bar to where the truck actually stops and an orange bar that runs off the end of the picture for the paved coast, a second (orange) truck coasting down the paved lane out of the picture, and three big read-outs: GRAVEL BED 133 m, PAVEMENT 3,184 m, 24x FARTHER (all from the simulation).
shots.narration_en: On pavement this truck would coast over three kilometers; the gravel stops it in about one hundred thirty meters.

shots.visual_proof: The truck (the same one) drives along the highway lane, swings off onto the ramp approach and heads for the gravel bed, under a big RUNAWAY TRUCK RAMP read-out; the last two seconds return to the opening ground-level camera with the truck charging in again, ending one frame before the film's first frame so the Short loops.
shots.narration_en: That is why steep mountain roads have ramps like this, waiting beside the highway for the next runaway truck.

first_three_seconds.note: Counts physical events becoming true and visible, not cuts or camera moves.

_edit_order_note: Shot order follows retention evidence from an earlier episode (steepest viewer loss at 3.5-6 s when the picture went from an event to an explanation; second loss at an 'and that is why' ending): the action macro follows the hook, the static cutaway moves to third and the ending loops back to the first frame.
